worksheet.title: Give Bit the Steps
worksheet.subtitle: Write the arrows to reach the star
worksheet.learning_goal: I can write the arrow steps that get Bit to the star.

parts.title: You make the plan
parts.text: Now YOU give Bit the steps. Look at where Bit is and where the star is. Draw one arrow for each box Bit must move. ➡ goes right, ⬅ goes left.

parts.title: Watch Bit — box 1 to the star on box 3
parts.note: Bit must move 2 boxes right. The steps are ➡ ➡.

parts.title: Box 1 to the star on box 4
parts.prompt: Bit is on box 1. The star is on box 4. Draw the arrows Bit needs (one per box).

parts.title: Box 2 to the star on box 3
parts.prompt: Bit is on box 2. The star is on box 3. Draw the arrows Bit needs.

parts.title: You try — go left
parts.prompt: Bit is on box 4. The star is on box 2. Draw the arrows Bit needs (this time the star is to the left).

parts.title: Big idea
parts.text: When you write the steps that solve a problem, you have made an algorithm. That is exactly what coders do!

teacher_guide.title: Give Bit the Steps
teacher_guide.subtitle: Quick facilitation notes & answer key
teacher_guide.footer_topic: 7. Give Bit the Steps — Teacher Guide

parts.title: Goal
parts.text: Children compose a short arrow program that moves Bit to the star — choosing the direction and the number of steps. Writing the steps that solve a problem is composing a simple algorithm (the create level of sequencing).

parts.title: Kindergarten frame (Ontario)
text: Problem Solving and Innovating — children create a sequence of directions to reach a goal.
No reading required of the child: read each prompt aloud; the child draws ➡/⬅ arrows in the boxes.

parts.title: Materials
parts.text: The printed worksheet + a pencil. Optional: floor boxes so children walk and then record the steps they took.

parts.title: Run it (about 15 min)
text: 1. MODEL: box 1 to the star on box 3 — 'two boxes right, so ➡ ➡.' Count the gap, then write that many arrows.
2. GUIDED: Exercise 1 — box 1 to box 4 is three boxes right → ➡ ➡ ➡.
3. YOU TRY: one step (Ex 2 → ➡), then a left move (Ex 3 → ⬅ ⬅).
4. Connect: 'Writing the steps that solve a problem is making an algorithm — that is what coders do.'

parts.title: Watch for & differentiate
text: Common slip: too many or too few arrows — count the boxes between Bit and the star first.
Simplify: do only right-moving goals before introducing the left move.
Extend: place the star farther away (box 5) and write the longer program.
Movement option: a child walks the route and the class records one arrow per step.

parts.title: Success looks like
parts.text: The child draws the correct number of arrows in the correct direction so the program reaches the star.
